routing_warnings.description: The requested page-two wording corrections concern report copy rather than the scannability of the page-one result explanation.
The RR04 wording changes concern risk-appropriate copy for the lower-exposure variant rather than the page-one result-explanation format.
The separate instruction to restore the missing standard footer on page 4 belongs to the page-footer Requirement.
The complaint that only Word documents were delivered concerns the independently required deliverable formats, not whether customer-specific fields are editable within a template.

The request for editable Canva templates belongs to the Canva deliverable Requirement; the generic approval of prior amendments is not concrete target-specific verification of every editable customer field.
The freelancer's delivery claim concerns the Word and Canva artifact formats rather than verification of customer-field editing behavior.
The clauses about incorrect page-one report IDs and header/footer codes concern per-variant report-code consistency rather than the exposure-level variant mapping.
The requested RR04 narrative amendments concern exposure-appropriate report copy rather than the existence or mapping of the four report variants.
The RR02 and RR03 false-confidence wording amendment belongs to risk-appropriate narrative copy.
The working and missing RR01–RR04 links concern delivery of editable Canva templates, not the report variant set itself.
The reported header defects concern incorrect per-variant RR identifiers rather than the header's presence or visual treatment.
The statement that internal headers now seem correct follows the per-variant code corrections and is evidence for report-code consistency.
The reported footer defect concerns incorrect RR identifiers in specific report variants, which is owned by the per-variant report-code Requirement rather than footer layout and coverage.
The remaining footer problem is specifically that RR02–RR04 still display RR-01, so it belongs to per-variant report-code consistency.
The incorrect exposure titles for RR02–RR04 concern the mapping of report variants to exposure levels.
The incorrect RR identifiers in internal headers belong to the dedicated internal-header code Requirement.
The incorrect RR identifiers in footers belong to the dedicated footer-code Requirement.
The client's observation that internal-header codes now appear correct is verification for the dedicated internal-header code Requirement.
The continuing RR-01 footer codes in RR02–RR04 are a runtime failure for the dedicated footer-code Requirement.
The requested RR04 narrative replacements concern exposure-appropriate report copy rather than report identifiers.
The missing footer on page 4 concerns footer presence across pages rather than the report code displayed in the footer.
